title: Refs and DOM Applied Check
description: Practice safe DOM access, mutable refs, forwarding refs, imperative handles, and ref-related pitfalls.
author: DailyCoder

questions.prompt: A component needs to focus an input after the user clicks "Edit". What is a good approach?

options.text: Attach a ref to the input and call inputRef.current.focus() in the click handler after checking it exists
Query the entire document during render
Store focus in state and expect the browser to focus automatically
Mutate the JSX object

questions.explanation: Focusing is an imperative DOM action that fits an event handler plus a DOM ref.

questions.prompt: You need to store a timeout id so cleanup can clear it, but the id should not render. What should you use?

options.text: useRef
useState
Context
React.memo

questions.explanation: A ref is appropriate for mutable bookkeeping that does not affect UI.

questions.prompt: Which patterns avoid unsafe DOM access? (Select all that apply.)

options.text: Check ref.current before using it
Measure layout in an effect or layout-aware callback rather than during render
Assume Strict Mode attaches refs exactly once
Clean up third-party DOM integrations

questions.explanation: Refs can be null, layout reads need committed DOM, and integrations should be cleaned up.

questions.prompt: A design-system Input wraps an HTML input. Parent components need to focus it. What API decision is needed?

options.text: Forward the ref or expose a focused imperative handle
Tell parents to use document.querySelector
Make the input global
Convert all props to context

questions.explanation: Reusable components must intentionally decide whether and how to expose ref access.

questions.prompt: useImperativeHandle is a good fit for exposing a small focus() method instead of the whole DOM node.

options.text: True
False

questions.explanation: A narrow imperative API can hide implementation details and reduce coupling.

questions.prompt: A component reads ref.current.offsetWidth during render to choose what to display. What is the problem?

options.text: The DOM may not be committed yet and render should stay pure
offsetWidth is always a string
Refs cannot point to DOM nodes
React requires class components for measurement

questions.explanation: DOM measurement should happen after commit, often using an effect, ResizeObserver, or layout effect when appropriate.

questions.prompt: Which values should usually be state instead of refs? (Select all that apply.)

options.text: Whether a details panel is open and rendered
Current input text shown in the UI
An interval id used only for cleanup
A previous value used only for comparison inside an effect

questions.explanation: Values that affect rendered output should be state; hidden mutable bookkeeping can be refs.

questions.prompt: A HOC wraps a component but does not forward refs. What happens to a parent ref passed to the wrapped export?

options.text: It points to the wrapper or is not delivered to the inner component as intended
It automatically reaches the inner DOM node
It becomes context
It triggers a re-render every time current changes

questions.explanation: Refs are not normal props; wrappers must explicitly forward them when ref access is part of the API.
